Thank you for the update; I have noted the infant was born at 32 weeks gestation via cesarean section to a mother with gestational diabetes. Given the prematurity and maternal history, could you describe the specific nature of the respiratory distress, such as grunting, nasal flaring, or chest retractions?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Gas_Analysis: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mm Hg (elevated), PaO2 60 mm Hg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5. Chest_X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity (32 weeks gestation). The clinical picture of ground-glass opacities and air bronchograms on the chest X-ray, combined with acidosis and hypercapnia on the blood gas analysis, confirms this diagnosis. Given the maternal history of gestational diabetes, I also recommend checking the blood glucose level to rule in or out Hypoglycemia, which can exacerbate respiratory issues.
